newsitem.title: USA: First images from Pathfinder reach Earth.
newsitem.headline: First images from Pathfinder reach Earth.

text.p: The Mars Pathfinder sent its first images back to earth on Friday, more then six hours after the unmanned space probe landed on the Red Planet.
NASA scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory here cheered when the black and white images were displayed.
The images showed parts of the solar panels of the Pathfinder as well as deflated airbags that were used to cushion the craft when it slammed into Mars.
In one frame, scientists could see the terrain of Mars and a shadow as the Sun rose over Mars.

The images capped what so far has been a better-than-expected day for NASA and JPL scientists. Earlier, Pathfinder made a picture-perfect landing on Mars. Later Friday the black and white images of the Red Planet are expected to be compiled into a color photo.

The Pathfinder's landing set the stage for an unprecedented exploration of the planet by a dune-buggy type vehicle called the "Soujourner", which will be driven by remote control from Earth as it conducts a one-week survey to chart the composition and size of Martian rocks, dust and debris.
